(The problem with most AI)

95%

95% of enterprise generative-AI pilots deliver no measurable return. The models aren't the problem. Understanding the problem is.

  1. 01

    Nobody asked the users

    Tools get chosen before anyone talks to the customers and staff who'll live with them.

  2. 02

    Generic tools

    Off-the-shelf assistants that never learn how your business actually works.

  3. 03

    Built for a demo

    Pilots on sample data that never touch a real system or a real customer, so they never ship.

The fix isn't a better model. Good User Experience (UX) design has always started with research, and AI is no different. Projects delivered with specialist partners reach production about twice as often as internal builds.

(Problems we solve)

Start with the problem.
Not the technology.

Some problems need a better website or a clearer journey. Some need automation. Most need both. These are the ones we hear most often when we talk to customers and staff.

  • Website01

    “The website looks fine, but it doesn't convert and nobody knows why.”

    What we build

    Research with real customers, a redesigned journey and a site built to be measured, with an assistant to answer questions out of hours.

    What we measure

    Conversion · enquiries

  • Service journeys02

    “Customers phone because the online form is too confusing to finish.”

    What we build

    A simplified, accessible journey designed and tested with users, with automation doing the checks behind the scenes.

    What we measure

    Completion rate · call volume

  • Customer support03

    “Tickets pile up overnight and the same forty questions eat the team's day.”

    What we build

    A support agent inside your helpdesk that resolves routine tickets, drafts the rest and hands off to a human with full context.

    What we measure

    First-response time · resolution rate

  • Internal tools04

    “Staff juggle five systems and a spreadsheet to finish one task.”

    What we build

    One well-designed internal tool, with automation doing the copying, checking and chasing in the background.

    What we measure

    Time per task · errors

  • Finance ops05

    “Invoices arrive in a dozen formats and month-end is a spreadsheet marathon.”

    What we build

    Document extraction, matching against POs and an exception queue that writes straight into your finance system.

    What we measure

    Days to close · cost per invoice

  • Reporting06

    “Data lives in six systems and nobody trusts the weekly report.”

    What we build

    Automated pipelines and a clear dashboard, plus an assistant that answers questions in plain English with the numbers to back it.

    What we measure

    Hours to report · data errors

(How we work)

Listen. Design.
Build. Improve.

The same user-centred process behind 25 years of design work, now applied to AI. Each stage has a clear exit, so you can stop after any of them and still walk away with something useful.

  1. 011–2 weeks

    Listen

    We talk to your customers, your staff and your leadership, and map how work really happens. You get a clear, costed plan, even if the answer is a better form rather than AI.

  2. 022–4 weeks

    Design

    We prototype the solution: the interface, the journey and the automation behind it. Then we test it with real users and your real data before anything is built.

  3. 034–8 weeks

    Build

    Production build inside your stack: websites, tools, integrations and AI agents, with guardrails and human handoff where it matters.

  4. 04Ongoing

    Improve

    We measure what changed, monitor every automation on HALO™ and keep refining with fresh feedback from your users.

(Questions)

Straight
answers.

Do you only do AI?+

No. Plenty of problems are solved by a clearer website, a simpler form or a better internal tool. We recommend AI only where it beats the alternatives, and we design the interface around it either way.

How is this different from buying an AI tool?+

Tools are built for the average company. We start with your customers, your process and your systems, then design only what moves your metric. Sometimes that includes an off-the-shelf tool, set up properly.

Do we need perfect data first?+

No. Discovery tells you what's usable today. Much of the early value comes from structuring the messy documents, inboxes and spreadsheets you already have.

Is our data safe?+

We work under UK GDPR, sign your DPA, keep data in your chosen region and never use it to train shared models. Access is least-privilege and every automated action is logged.

What if the prototype doesn't work?+

Then you find out in weeks, not quarters, and you don't proceed to the build. The decision is made against the metric we agreed in writing.

Who looks after it once it's live?+

You choose: we hand over with documentation and training, or keep running it on HALO™ with a monthly improvement cycle.
